content.comment_body: Hello, does anyone know how to create a button in the [product_name] Web Editor? The digital outputs are currently set to 'Switch Mode'. How can I make them work like buttons instead? Thanks.

Hi, could you provide a sketch or image showing what you have in mind for the button? Uploading an example would help clarify your request. Based on my understanding, you want to control ON/OFF (such as a bit: M1) via the webserver, which would require writing to it. I've attached a screenshot from a sample project that shows how to make an object writable. Hope that helps.

Using digital values in the self-designed websites of [product_name] Web Editor, it isn't possible to set up a pushbutton function directly. However, you can use a workaround in the [product_name] program logic. Assign a bit in the memory area (for example, V0.1), and use it as network input. Simultaneously, configure a network output with the same address (V0.1) to reset it with a LOW signal. This setup works so that when the digital value is clicked, the web server writes a 1 to the bit, triggering a pulse relay, which then writes 0 back to reset it—simulating a momentary button press. See the attached image for reference.
It was clear to me that you meant a 'push button function'.
I usually use a similar workaround.
Hi [user_name], thanks. Instead of the output Q, I switched to using a pulse relay. It worked perfectly after I added an off-delay to lengthen the signal.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are finding it difficult to implement momentary pushbutton functionality for digital values using the [product_name] Web Editor, as it only provides toggle switch control. To work around this limitation, users create custom logic configurations in the [product_name] program to mimic button behavior, resulting in additional setup and a more complex solution. This lack of built-in support for pushbutton actions in the web interface leads to user frustration and sharing of unofficial solutions within the community.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect an option to configure digital controls in the [product_name] Web Editor as true pushbuttons, allowing for momentary actions directly from the web interface.
